lines.trans: Step right up, little brother! Smell that toasted brown sugar crust on Tin Two!

words.gloss: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)

lines.trans: It smells like a street festival, Tomas, though the top layer shines a lot.

words.gloss: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)

lines.trans: How many spoons of coarse sugar did you pour under the high heat of the oven, Tomas?
Enough so that every slice has a perfect crunchy snap when the fork goes down!
Let me press my dessert fork gently right in the middle... tap, tap, clang!
Oh my goodness, a cake should not ring like the front-desk bell, Tomas!
Speaking as an architect, with Tin Two we could roof the courtyard roof.
Hey! Break through that top window and taste the warm almond cake underneath!
Mmm, underneath that sugar helmet, the berries and ground almonds are delicious!
So lemon alone turns out too sour, and dry sugar alone turns into stone.
What soft, shiny glaze could be hiding beneath that blue ink smudge, Rocio?
Bring me that green plant book again: our nose will read better than our eyes!
Step right up, little brother! Smell that toasted brown sugar crust on Tin Two!

Enough so that every slice has a perfect crunchy snap when the fork goes down!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

acercar.gloss: to bring closer; to move closer

meanings.en: to bring closer; to move closer
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (acerqué, acerque).

examples.text: Acerca la lámpara a la mesa de trabajo, por favor.
examples.trans: Bring the lamp closer to the workbench, please.

examples.text: Acercamos dos sillas de madera junto al piano.
examples.trans: We move two wooden chairs closer to the piano.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Classic Mediterranean baking ingredient in tarts and biscuits.

examples.text: Rocío hornea galletas crujientes de almendra y limón.
examples.trans: Rocio bakes crunchy almond and lemon biscuits.

examples.text: Tostamos las almendras cinco minutos en el horno.
examples.trans: We toast the almonds for five minutes in the oven.

apoyar.gloss: to lean; to rest; to support

meanings.en: to lean; to rest; to support
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; apoyar algo contra la pared means 'to lean something against the wall'.

examples.text: Apoya la escalera con cuidado contra el ladrillo.
examples.trans: Lean the ladder carefully against the brick.

examples.text: Apoyamos las sillas dobladas debajo del arco.
examples.trans: We lean the folded chairs under the arch.

meanings.note: Feminine: la arquitecta.

examples.text: El arquitecto está aquí.
examples.trans: The architect is here.

examples.text: Vemos los arquitectos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the architects from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.text: Las habitaciones están arriba.
examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.

examples.text: Mira arriba hacia el balcón.
examples.trans: Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Así que means 'so / therefore'.

examples.text: Hazlo así, despacio.
examples.trans: Do it like this, slowly.

examples.text: Llueve mucho, así que entramos.
examples.trans: It is raining hard, so let us go inside.

meanings.note: Takes indicative for known facts and subjunctive for hypotheticals.

examples.text: Salimos aunque llueve un poco.
examples.trans: We are going out even though it is raining a bit.

examples.text: Esperaré aquí aunque tarde diez minutos.
examples.trans: I will wait here even if he takes ten minutes.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, sympathy, or mild dismay.

examples.text: ¡Ay, casi olvido el paraguas!
examples.trans: Oh, I nearly forgot my umbrella!

examples.text: ¡Ay, qué susto me has dado!
examples.trans: Goodness, what a fright you gave me!

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.text: Es una pieza azul.
examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Commonly masculine (sin azúcar = without sugar).

examples.text: El azúcar es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The sugar is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el azúcar.
examples.trans: We talk about the sugar.

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.en: to go down; to bring down; to lower
meanings.note: Works both intransitively (go downstairs) and transitively (bring down).

examples.text: Bajo a la cocina a preparar té.
examples.trans: I go down to the kitchen to make tea.

examples.text: Bajamos las maletas por la escalera.
examples.trans: We bring the suitcases down the stairs.

meanings.note: Bajo llave means 'under lock and key'; as an adjective (bajo/baja), means 'low' or 'ground' (planta baja).

examples.text: Nos sentamos bajo el limonero.
examples.trans: We sit under the lemon tree.

examples.text: Guarda la caja bajo llave.
examples.trans: Keep the box under lock and key.

meanings.note: General botanical and culinary word for small fleshy berries (bayas rojas = red berries).

examples.text: Tomás lavó dos cestas llenas de bayas rojas maduras.
examples.trans: Tomas washed two baskets full of ripe red berries.

examples.text: Las bayas dulces combinan muy bien con la masa de almendra.
examples.trans: Sweet berries pair very well with the almond batter.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: El suelo está limpio y brillante.
examples.trans: The floor is clean and shiny.

examples.text: Tiene unos ojos brillantes.
examples.trans: She has bright eyes.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb for light, polished wood or eyes.

examples.text: El sol brilla sobre el patio.
examples.trans: The sun shines over the courtyard.

examples.text: Las estrellas brillan esta noche.
examples.trans: The stars are shining tonight.

meanings.note: Invariable before masculine or feminine singular nouns (cada día, cada mañana).

examples.text: Abro la cafetería cada mañana.
examples.trans: I open the cafe every morning.

examples.text: Cada habitación tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Each room has its own key.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.text: La calle está aquí.
examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Gate bell or church bell.

examples.text: La campana está aquí.
examples.trans: The bell is here.

examples.text: Vemos las campanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bells from the door.

meanings.note: Una capa de pintura means 'a coat of paint'.

examples.text: Mañana daremos la segunda capa de verde a las lamas.
examples.trans: Tomorrow we will give the slats their second coat of green.

examples.text: Extiende una capa fina de crema sobre la base.
examples.trans: Spread a thin layer of curd over the crust.

meanings.note: El casco antiguo is the historic old quarter of a Spanish city.

examples.text: El casco está aquí.
examples.trans: The historic centre is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cascos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the historic centres from the door.

meanings.note: El centro is downtown.

examples.text: El centro está aquí.
examples.trans: The city centre is here.

examples.text: Vemos los centros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the city centres from the door.

meanings.note: Onomatopoeia imitating a metallic ring against a hard surface.

examples.text: El tenedor de postre hizo ¡clanc! contra el azúcar tostado.
examples.trans: The dessert fork went clang! against the toasted sugar.

examples.text: Oímos un clanc fuerte cuando cayó la llave sobre la piedra.
examples.trans: We heard a loud clank when the key dropped onto the stone.

meanings.note: Unaccented como compares or gives a reason (distinct from interrogative cómo).

examples.text: Está fría como el agua del río.
examples.trans: It is as cold as river water.

examples.text: Todo funciona como debe ser.
examples.trans: Everything works just as it should.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Golden crust of bread or cake, or tree bark.

examples.text: La corteza está aquí.
examples.trans: The crust is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cortezas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the crusts from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza crujiente.
examples.trans: It is a crispy piece.

examples.text: ¡Hornea muchas esquinas crujientes, cariño!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, my dear!

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb in present and preterite, but has the irregular past participle cubierto ('covered').

examples.text: Alguien cubrió los lados del hueco con ladrillos rojos.
examples.trans: Someone lined the sides of the cavity with red bricks.

examples.text: Rocío cubre la masa con un paño limpio.
examples.trans: Rocío covers the dough with a clean cloth.

meanings.note: Table or soup spoon; cucharita is a teaspoon.

examples.text: Pon una cuchara limpia junto a cada cuenco.
examples.trans: Set a clean spoon beside each bowl.

examples.text: Prueba la sopa de lentejas con esta cuchara.
examples.trans: Taste the lentil soup with this spoon.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with its noun.

examples.text: ¿Cuántos bizcochos puedes hornear?
examples.trans: How many sponge cakes can you bake?

examples.text: ¿Cuánto tiempo tenemos antes de las doce?
examples.trans: How much time do we have before twelve?

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Debajo de + noun means 'underneath something'.

examples.text: Hay una llave pegada debajo.
examples.trans: There is a key taped underneath.

examples.text: Mira debajo de las ruedas.
examples.trans: Look underneath the wheels.

meanings.note: With a noun object (le debo la verdad), means 'to owe'; before an infinitive, means 'should / ought to'.

examples.text: Le debo diez euros de cambio.
examples.trans: I owe you ten euros in change.

examples.text: Todo funciona como debe ser.
examples.trans: Everything works as it should.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.

examples.text: Déjame ayudarte con esa caja.
examples.trans: Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

echar.gloss: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)

meanings.en: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)
meanings.note: Echar un vistazo = take a glance; echar de menos = miss someone.

examples.text: Echa un poco más de agua caliente.
examples.trans: Pour a little more hot water.

examples.text: Te he echado mucho de menos.
examples.trans: I have missed you very much.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Esconderse detrás de = to hide behind.

examples.text: Escondo el regalo en el armario.
examples.trans: I hide the present in the wardrobe.

examples.text: El gato se escondió detrás de la maceta.
examples.trans: The cat hid behind the flowerpot.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la fiesta'). The idiomatic phrase 'estar/ir de fiesta' means to be out partying.

examples.text: Aquí, de fiesta, cuéntame.
examples.trans: Right here, out partying, tell me what's up.

examples.text: Después del estreno organizaron una fiesta privada para todo el equipo.
examples.trans: After the premiere they threw a private party for the whole crew.

fuego.gloss: fire; stove heat (a fuego suave = over gentle heat)

meanings.en: fire; stove heat (a fuego suave = over gentle heat)
meanings.note: In the kitchen, el fuego means the burner/heat and a fuego lento / suave means 'on low / gentle heat'.

examples.text: Cuece la crema a fuego suave para que no se pegue.
examples.trans: Cook the custard over gentle heat so it does not stick.

examples.text: Retira el cazo del fuego antes de mezclar la mantequilla.
examples.trans: Take the saucepan off the heat before mixing in the butter.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (llover/discutir fuerte).

examples.text: Es una pieza fuerte.
examples.trans: It is a strong piece.

examples.text: ¡Rápido, ciérralo! Vamos a subirlo... esperad, ¿qué es ese golpe metálico tan fuerte?
examples.trans: Quick, close it! Let us take it upstairs... wait, what is that loud metallic bang?

meanings.note: Sweet lemon or sugar glaze.

examples.text: El glaseado es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The glaze is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el glaseado.
examples.trans: We talk about the glaze.

meanings.note: Describes thick envelopes, walls, or coats.

examples.text: Es una pieza gruesa.
examples.trans: It is a thick piece.

examples.text: este sobre grueso
examples.trans: this thick envelope

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Hablo con mi familia cada domingo.
examples.trans: I speak with my family every Sunday.

examples.text: Hablamos largo rato bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We talked for a long while under the tree.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Affectionate diminutive of hermano.

examples.text: El hermanito está aquí.
examples.trans: The little brother is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hermanitos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the little brothers from the door.

meanings.note: Del horno = out of the oven.

examples.text: El horno está aquí.
examples.trans: The oven is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hornos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ovens from the door.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.text: La llave está justo aquí.
examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Preterite 3rd sg/pl spells y: leyó, leyeron; past participle leído.

examples.text: Leo el periódico con el primer café.
examples.trans: I read the newspaper with my first coffee.

examples.text: Anoche leímos toda la carta juntos.
examples.trans: Last night we read the whole letter together.

meanings.note: Libro de reservas = reservation ledger.

examples.text: El libro está aquí.
examples.trans: The book is here.

examples.text: Vemos los libros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the books from the door.

meanings.note: Plural limones.

examples.text: El limón está aquí.
examples.trans: The lemon is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemons from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.

examples.text: ¡Hasta luego, que tengas buen día!
examples.trans: See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: ¡Madre mía! is a mild, warm everyday exclamation across Spain.

examples.text: La madre está aquí.
examples.trans: The mother is here.

examples.text: Vemos las madres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mothers from the door.

meanings.note: Everyday noun related to manchar ('to stain').

examples.text: Esa mancha fresca de pintura sale con agua templada.
examples.trans: That fresh smudge of paint comes out with warm water.

examples.text: Revisa que los manteles blancos no tengan ninguna mancha.
examples.trans: Check that the white tablecloths do not have a single stain.

meanings.note: Irregular comparative/superlative of bueno; plural mejores.

examples.text: Esta ventana tiene la mejor vista.
examples.trans: This window has the best view.

examples.text: Hoy el radiador calienta mejor.
examples.trans: Today the radiator heats better.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

mmm.gloss: mmm! (expression of pleasure when tasting or smelling food)

meanings.en: mmm! (expression of pleasure when tasting or smelling food)
meanings.note: Universal nasal interjection used when savouring a delicious flavour or aroma.

examples.text: ¡Mmm, la miga de almendra con bayas rojas está riquísima!
examples.trans: Mmm, the almond crumb with red berries is delicious!

examples.text: Mmm, ¡qué bien huele el pan recién salido del horno!
examples.trans: Mmm, how wonderful the bread fresh out of the oven smells!

meanings.note: In baking, el molde is a cake tin or baking pan; letra de molde means block/printed letters.

examples.text: Repartimos la masa de almendra en tres moldes redondos pequeños.
examples.trans: We divided the almond batter across three small round baking tins.

examples.text: Unta el molde con un poco de mantequilla antes de meterlo al horno.
examples.trans: Grease the baking tin with a little butter before putting it in the oven.

meanings.note: Past participle of moler ('to grind') used as a culinary adjective: almendra molida ('ground almonds'), café molido ('ground coffee').

examples.text: Mezcla doscientos gramos de almendra molida con mantequilla.
examples.trans: Mix two hundred grams of ground almonds with butter.

examples.text: Me encanta el aroma del café recién molido por la mañana.
examples.trans: I love the aroma of freshly ground coffee in the morning.

moreno.gloss: brown (azúcar moreno = brown sugar); dark-haired; sun-tanned

meanings.en: brown (azúcar moreno = brown sugar); dark-haired; sun-tanned
meanings.note: In cooking, azúcar moreno is unrefined brown cane sugar; for people, it means dark-haired or tanned.

examples.text: Tomás cubrió el segundo molde con una capa de azúcar moreno crujiente.
examples.trans: Tomas covered the second tin with a layer of crunchy brown sugar.

examples.text: ¿Prefieres endulzar el café con azúcar blanco o con azúcar moreno?
examples.trans: Do you prefer to sweeten your coffee with white sugar or brown sugar?

meanings.note: Superlative degree of mucho.

examples.text: Lo siento muchísimo, señora.
examples.trans: I am terribly sorry, madam.

examples.text: Me alegro muchísimo por ti.
examples.trans: I am so happy for you.

meanings.note: Shortened form of mucho used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.text: El bizcocho está muy rico.
examples.trans: The sponge cake is very tasty.

examples.text: Camina muy rápido por el puente.
examples.trans: She walks very fast across the bridge.

meanings.note: Plural las narices.

examples.text: La nariz está aquí.
examples.trans: The nose is here.

examples.text: Vemos las narices desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the noses from the door.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.text: Nuestra posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.

examples.text: Nuestros vecinos toman café aquí.
examples.trans: Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Plural los ojos.

examples.text: El ojo está aquí.
examples.trans: The eye is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ojos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the eyes from the door.

oler.gloss: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)

meanings.en: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)
meanings.note: Irregular boot stem hue- (huelo, hueles, huele, huelen).

examples.text: La cocina huele a canela caliente.
examples.trans: The kitchen smells like warm cinnamon.

examples.text: El jardín huele a flores frescas.
examples.trans: The garden smells of fresh flowers.

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.text: ¿Quiere otra taza de café?
examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.text: ¿Me oyes bien por teléfono?
examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: El patio está aquí.
examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Used alone as 'Perfect!'.

examples.text: Es una pieza perfecta.
examples.trans: It is a perfect piece.

examples.text: La clienta de la habitación cuatro se queda toda la semana. ¡Todo debe estar perfecto!
examples.trans: The guest in room four is staying all week. Everything must be perfect!

meanings.note: De piedra = made of stone.

examples.text: La piedra está aquí.
examples.trans: The stone is here.

examples.text: Vemos las piedras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stones from the door.

meanings.note: Planta baja = ground floor; primera planta = first floor; also a green plant.

examples.text: La planta está aquí.
examples.trans: The floor / storey is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floor / storeys from the door.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.text: ¿Puedo ver la etiqueta otra vez?
examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Standard word for the sweet course at the end of a meal (de postre = for dessert; tenedor de postre = dessert fork).

examples.text: De postre vamos a servir tarta tibia de almendra con bayas rojas.
examples.trans: For dessert we are going to serve warm almond and red berry cake.

examples.text: Mateo cogió un tenedor pequeño de postre para probar el glaseado.
examples.trans: Mateo picked up a small dessert fork to test the glaze.

probar.gloss: to try; to taste; to test

meanings.en: to try; to taste; to test
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: pruebo).

examples.text: Prueba este pan con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: Try this bread with olive oil.

examples.text: Ayer probamos la mermelada de manzana.
examples.trans: Yesterday we tasted the apple jam.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.text: Solo quedan dos habitaciones libres.
examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: En recepción = at the front desk.

examples.text: La recepción está aquí.
examples.trans: The front desk is here.

examples.text: Vemos las recepciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the front desks from the door.

meanings.note: With food and drink, ¡qué rico! is the most natural Spanish way to say 'how delicious!'.

examples.text: Esta tarta casera de limón está muy rica.
examples.trans: This homemade lemon tart is delicious.

examples.text: La miel de otoño tiene un sabor rico y suave.
examples.trans: Autumn honey has a rich, smooth flavour.

meanings.note: Regular verb with irregular past participle roto.

examples.text: Ten cuidado de no romper la taza.
examples.trans: Be careful not to break the cup.

examples.text: El viento rompió una rama seca.
examples.trans: The wind snapped a dry branch.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Toallas secas = dry towels.

examples.text: Es una pieza seca.
examples.trans: It is a dry piece.

examples.text: ¡Javier lo dejó ahí cuando cogió la toalla seca!
examples.trans: Javier set it down there when he took the dry towel!

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.text: Solo necesito cinco minutos más.
examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.

examples.text: Queda una sola habitación libre.
examples.trans: Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza suave.
examples.trans: It is a soft piece.

examples.text: Y mire: esta chaqueta de lana suave está limpia y nueva. Pruébela.
examples.trans: And look: this soft wool cardigan is clean and unworn. Try it on.

meanings.note: Agrees in number with the noun it modifies (suficiente luz, suficientes cucharas).

examples.text: Tenemos suficientes pinzas de madera para las veintiocho servilletas.
examples.trans: We have enough wooden clothespins for all twenty-eight napkins.

examples.text: Dos cucharadas de miel son suficientes para cubrir toda la tarta.
examples.trans: Two tablespoons of honey are enough to cover the whole cake.

meanings.note: Onomatopoeia for a light, crisp tap against wood, glass, or a hard crust (also in tic-tac = tick-tock).

examples.text: El tenedor hizo ¡tac, tac! contra la capa dura de azúcar tostado.
examples.trans: The fork went tap, tap! against the hard layer of toasted sugar.

examples.text: En el silencio del taller solo se oía el tic-tac del reloj antiguo.
examples.trans: In the silence of the workshop you could only hear the tick-tock of the old clock.

meanings.note: Usual word in Spain for a sweet tart or birthday cake.

examples.text: Hay tarta de chocolate para el postre.
examples.trans: There is chocolate cake for dessert.

examples.text: Mi abuela hace una tarta de manzana riquísima.
examples.trans: My grandmother makes a delicious apple tart.

meanings.note: Sloping exterior roof covered in tiles.

examples.text: El tejado está aquí.
examples.trans: The tiled roof is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tejados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tiled roofs from the door.

meanings.note: Standard word for an eating fork (tenedor de postre = dessert fork).

examples.text: Mateo se llevó un tenedor lleno de tarta tibia a la boca.
examples.trans: Mateo put a forkful of warm cake into his mouth.

examples.text: Coloca el tenedor a la izquierda del plato y el cuchillo a la derecha.
examples.trans: Place the fork to the left of the plate and the knife to the right.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Describes a gentle, pleasant warmth (pan tibio, agua tibia), similar to templado.

examples.text: El pan recién salido del horno todavía está tibio y tierno.
examples.trans: The bread fresh from the oven is still warm and soft.

examples.text: Disuelve la levadura en medio vaso de agua tibia.
examples.trans: Dissolve the yeast in half a glass of lukewarm water.

meanings.note: Con tinta permanente = in permanent ink.

examples.text: La tinta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The ink is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la tinta.
examples.trans: We talk about the ink.

tocar.gloss: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)

meanings.en: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: toqué.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: Someone just rang the bell.

examples.text: De niño tocaba el piano los viernes.
examples.trans: As a boy he played the piano on Fridays.

tostar.gloss: to toast; to roast; to brown

meanings.en: to toast; to roast; to brown
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue); past participle tostado ('toasted, roasted').

examples.text: Huele qué bien se ha tostado el azúcar moreno en el segundo molde.
examples.trans: Smell how nicely the brown sugar has toasted in the second tin.

examples.text: Rocío tuesta las almendras en láminas unos minutos en la sartén.
examples.trans: Rocio toasts the sliced almonds for a few minutes in the pan.

meanings.note: Irregular: traigo, traje; future traeré.

examples.text: Ahora mismo le traigo una cuchara.
examples.trans: I will bring you a spoon right now.

examples.text: Ayer trajo flores del mercado.
examples.trans: Yesterday she brought flowers from the market.

meanings.note: Un trozo de bizcocho = a piece of cake.

examples.text: El trozo está aquí.
examples.trans: The piece is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trozos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pieces from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.text: La ventana está aquí.
examples.trans: The window is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza verde.
examples.trans: It is a green piece.

examples.text: Mateo, ¿me oyes? ¡Acabo de pasar la farmacia verde!
examples.trans: Mateo, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.text: La vez está aquí.
examples.trans: The time / occasion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las veces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the time / occasions from the door.

volver.gloss: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)

meanings.en: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: vuelvo), past participle vuelto; volverse + adj = become.

examples.text: Vuelvo en cinco minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in five minutes.

examples.text: Volvió a sonreír enseguida.
examples.trans: He smiled again right away.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Standard word for the sharp, tart taste of lemons or unripe fruit.

examples.text: El primer molde lleva un glaseado de zumo ácido de limón.
examples.trans: The first tin has a tart lemon-juice glaze.

examples.text: La miel tibia se mantiene suave sin volverse ácida en el horno.
examples.trans: Warm honey stays smooth without turning sour in the oven.
